standard_prerequisites.use: The definition of etale-local-on-source-and-target for properties of germs (Descent) and its etale-on-fibres lemma, plus the henselization-CM equivalence (More on Algebra); cited inputs with the argument written in the retained span.

core_obligations: Start from a diagram as in the Descent definition of source-and-target etale locality for germs.
Observe the induced morphism of fibres is etale and carries u' to u.
Identify the strict henselizations of the two fibre local rings.
Transfer Noetherian Cohen-Macaulayness via the henselization-CM lemma.

proof_roadmap.step: Pass to the etale morphism of fibres and identify strict henselizations.
Conclude via henselization invariance of the Noetherian CM property.

difficulty_reason: For morphisms of germs of algebraic spaces (X, x) -> (S, s), the property that the local ring O_{X_s, x} of the fibre is Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay is etale local on the source-and-target in the pointed sense of the Descent chapter. The retained proof is written out: in a source-and-target etale diagram, the induced morphism of fibres U'_{v'} -> U_v is etale and maps u' to u (Descent lemma on etale maps of fibres), hence the strict henselizations of O_{U'_{v'}, u'} and O_{U_v, u} agree, and the more-algebra lemma that the henselization of a local ring is Cohen-Macaulay exactly when the ring is (Noetherian likewise) transfers the property. Retained author proof at lines 6205-6215.
